review.review: The run ended in planner exhaustion, not an observed death; the terminal hero had 25/25 HP. Decision 282 (log line 806) publicly showed an upgrade scroll behind magical fire while an identified frost potion was carried. Decisions 282–284 selected exploration rather than extinguishing. The selecting chain explains this contradiction: Mage preparation yields whenever priority loot remains (tools/mage_policy.py:1134–1138); the priority pickup helper delegates to potion preparation, which skips already-known frost (tools/puzzle_supplies.py:448–467), leaving the existing extinguisher unreachable. At decision 300 (lines 860–861), fire-buffer exclusions still blocked the reward and mandatory pickup correctly prevented descent. This is an arbitration defect, not proof of an impossible room. The proposed repair lets that priority helper call the existing guarded extinguisher for inaccessible permanent progression loot, without overriding active room workflows. A new condensed public-evidence fixture failed two assertions on original source and passes all six tests with the repair; the full suite passes 1620 tests with four skips. This is fixture validation, not reconstructed recorded memory or a gameplay replay. It establishes selection of preparation, not successful extinguishing, collection, or survival.
review.learnings: Mandatory progression loot can require using a known puzzle supply, not identifying another potion. A priority pickup controller must retain access to that guarded preparation instead of excluding it through its own obligation. Preserve observed pickup receipts, hazard buffers, potion identity checks and the planner-exhaustion outcome.
